name: Thirteen

notes.2: Three face-down hands of 17 — you pick one each, and the third is set aside.

tagline: Beat it, bomb it, or pass.
howToPlay: The 2 is the highest card in the game and the 3 is the lowest, which is the opposite of nearly every other game on this shelf. Suits break every tie — spades lowest, then clubs, diamonds, hearts — so no two cards are equal and there is always an answer or a pass. The lowest card in play leads the first hand and the lead has to contain it, which is the 3♠ at a full table and whatever survived the deal at a short one.

By default a pass only skips your turn and you are asked again when the play comes back round. Switch off "Passing keeps you in the trick" for the stricter rule, where a pass puts you out of the trick for good and passing early to keep a run together is a real decision rather than a shrug.

The bombs are the point of the game. Three consecutive pairs kill a lone 2, four of a kind kills a pair of them, and a chop can itself be chopped — which is why holding the highest card in the deck is not the free win the ladder makes it look.

Two-handed, the deal is different. Dealing thirteen each would leave half the deck unseen by anybody, so instead the whole pack goes into three face-down hands of seventeen (with one odd card set aside) and you take one each — the third hand sits out. Whoever lost the last hand picks first, and the first hand of a match is a coin toss; the lowest card in play still leads either way, so the pick and the lead tend to fall on opposite sides of the table.

variants.name: Passing keeps you in the trick
variants.description: A pass only skips your turn — you are asked again when the play comes back round, instead of being out of the trick for good.

variants.name: A 2 can end a run
variants.description: Q-K-A-2 is a run. It still never wraps round to the 3, a 2 is still no part of consecutive pairs, and a dragon is still 3-to-A.

variants.name: Instant wins
variants.description: Four 2s, six pairs, a 3-to-A dragon, five consecutive pairs or three consecutive triples end the hand on the deal.

variants.name: No ending on a pig
variants.description: A 2 may not be the last card you play, so a won position can become a trap.

variants.name: A pair of pigs needs four pairs
variants.description: Four of a kind no longer chops a pair of 2s — only four consecutive pairs will do it.
